summary: Lornoxicam is a potent oxicam-class NSAID used for short-term relief of acute pain (including postoperative) and symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. The usual dose is 8-16 mg/day in divided doses (maximum 16 mg). As an NSAID it carries cardiovascular thrombotic and GI bleeding/ulcer risks. It is not FDA-approved.
indications: Short-term treatment of acute mild to moderate pain
Symptomatic relief of pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis
Symptomatic relief of pain and inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis

dosage.n: Increased risk of GI/renal adverse effects

admin: Take with or after food, or with a full glass of water, to reduce GI irritation
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time
Do not combine with other NSAIDs
Consider gastroprotection (PPI) in patients at GI risk
Ensure adequate hydration to protect renal function
moa: Lornoxicam non-selectively inhibits cyclo-oxygenase enzymes COX-1 and COX-2, reducing synthesis of prostaglandins that mediate inflammation, pain and fever. It has potent analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity with a relatively short half-life.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to lornoxicam or other NSAIDs (including aspirin-induced asthma/urticaria)
Active peptic ulcer or GI bleeding
Severe hepatic or severe renal impairment
Coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery period
relative: History of peptic ulcer or GI bleeding

preg: Avoid - NSAIDs can cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus and impair fetal renal function, and are contraindicated in the third trimester. Avoid in first/second trimester unless clearly necessary.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; data are limited and NSAID exposure to the infant is best avoided.
renal: Avoid in moderate to severe renal impairment. Use with caution and monitor renal function in mild impairment, dehydration, or with nephrotoxic co-medication.
hepatic: Reduce dose in mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment and avoid in severe impairment; monitor liver enzymes.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) and antiplatelets - markedly increased bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity
Methotrexate - reduced clearance and increased toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal risk (triple whammy)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; food slightly slows absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - increases the risk of GI bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise creatinine/liver enzymes and prolong bleeding time.

monitoring: Renal function and blood pressure, especially in at-risk patients
Hemoglobin and signs of GI bleeding with prolonged use
Liver enzymes if used longer term
Cardiovascular status in patients with CV risk
counsel: Take with food and use for the shortest time needed
Stop and seek care for black stools, vomiting blood, or severe stomach pain
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory painkillers
Report chest pain, breathlessness, ankle swelling or reduced urination
Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners, lithium or methotrexate
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), protect from moisture
pearls: Potent short-half-life oxicam NSAID - useful for acute and postoperative pain
Shares NSAID class risks: GI bleeding, cardiovascular thrombotic events, renal impairment
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration; max 16 mg/day
Avoid in severe renal/hepatic impairment, active ulcer and third-trimester pregnancy
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not double up. For short courses, only take when needed for pain.
overdose: Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, drowsiness, and in severe cases renal failure or seizures. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, gastric decontamination if early, and gastroprotection. Hemodialysis is not effective due to high protein binding.
